action: Read the existing parameter in memory, validate its exact format and version twice, update only primary from resend to ses while preserving the Resend key, then verify version 2 and unchanged remaining fields. Submit secret-bearing input via an anonymous memory descriptor. Never print or persist its value.
effect: The shared route is used by both notification emails and Identity verification/reset emails. SES becomes primary and Resend stays fallback. Existing verified domain and production SES access were observed. Existing provider caches refresh on their existing schedule, up to four hours.
safety: The helper refuses a changed version or unexpected content. SSM does not offer atomic compare-and-swap here; the second read narrows but does not eliminate concurrent-change risk. Stop and investigate any ambiguous write or unexpected result; no automatic retry or key rotation.
resource_preservation: Leave all existing host, database and other resources running. No API deployment, email send, DNS change, resource destruction, key rotation or other parameter write is authorized.
approval: Explicit approval of this exact plan SHA-256 is required for the SSM parameter write.
